**Triage — sweep ③ lane repair.** Added `priority:p2` · `domain:services` · `i18n`; `needs-user-decision` kept. ⛔ No decision content added — the ruling is the maintainer's.

**Anchor**: the ADR-0092 D2 whitelist is `getManagedUpdateWhitelist('sys_user')`, pinned at `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/identity-write-guard.test.ts:181` as exactly `new Set(['name', 'image'])`. The guard it pins lives in the same directory, so whichever way this is ruled the change lands in `packages/plugins/plugin-auth`. ⇒ `domain:services`. ✅ Whitelist contents confirmed at `origin/main` — the card's "stays `{name, image}`" is accurate today, not a recollection.

**`p2`** for the same reason as its sibling: it gates queued work. **#14762** is `pm:blocked` partly on this, and **#13881** is `pm:dispatched` on the column.

⚠️ ⛔ **Do not rule this one in isolation from #14788.** The two are coupled in one direction that is easy to miss: this card decides *who may write* the column, but that answer determines what the column **means** — an administered value or a user-stated preference — and #14788's precedence question ("does the stored locale outrank the request's `Accept-Language`?") has a different right answer in each case. A stored value the user cannot set is weaker evidence of intent than the `Accept-Language` the browser just sent; a value the user chose is stronger. Ruling them separately can produce a pair that does not compose.

⚠️ Also recorded, measured this round: **#13881 has not landed** (`git grep 13881 -- packages/` → **0** at `origin/main`). The card's "column lands `readonly`" describes that branch's design, not `main`'s state — so the whitelist is not merely unchanged, there is as yet no column for it to have excluded.

## Maintainer ruling recorded — B: a user may set their own `sys_user.locale`; the ADR-0092 D2 self-service whitelist becomes `{name, image, locale}`

Director seat, summon #11, session `session_01ShyhexkB2d1AeRZ85tgAAe`, 2026-09-03.

Provenance (who / verbatim / where): maintainer, live PM chat with the director seat, 2026-09-03, replying to decision batch #18 in which this card was item 2 with the recommendation B (fallback A), presented together with #14788 (item 1) because the two compose; the batch stated the composition explicitly — under B the stored locale is a user-stated preference and outranks the request's `Accept-Language` when set. Verbatim reply: 「同意」 — adopts B, and D on #14788.

**Ruled: B.** The identity table's user-writable set grows from two fields to three — a security-boundary act taken by the maintainer and recorded as such. `SYS_USER_PROFILE_EDIT_FIELDS` becomes `{name, image, locale}`; `MANAGED_EXTENSION_EDITABLE_FIELDS.sys_user` gains `locale`; the column's `readonly` goes; the `identity-write-guard` and `managed-extension-fields` pins are flipped rather than deleted. A malformed value is refused loudly by the column's BCP-47 shape check (`LOCALE_TAG_SHAPE`) and never dead-letters a notification; the deployment default remains the fallback for an unset column. Option A (system-context writes only) is not taken — it would make every application build its own stamping route.

Execution: `domain:services` lane (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth`), M, **after PR #14775 (#13881) has merged**. **`Clause-②: yes`** (a published write path accepts a field it refused before) ⇒ contract-review tier, `needs:contract-review`, in-seat review. The services seat files the objectui card for the "my language" form item (`Blocked-by:` this card) so the setting is reachable from the platform's own UI, and notes in the PR body that #14788's endpoint precedence (`sys_user.locale` when set → `Accept-Language` → deployment default) is the reading side of this write.

State transition, same stroke: `needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue`. Ledger: director seat post #12708, summon #11.

**Comments read to the last page before dispatch: 2.** Ruling of record: **comment 5522882528** — maintainer ruling **B**, adopted verbatim 「同意」, recorded by the director seat (summon #11, session `session_01ShyhexkB2d1AeRZ85tgAAe`). A user **may** set their own `sys_user.locale`; the ADR-0092 D2 self-service whitelist becomes `{name, image, locale}`. Option A (system-context writes only) is explicitly not taken.

**The ruling's stated prerequisite is satisfied, and this seat verified it rather than inferring it.** The ruling sequences execution "**after PR #14775 (#13881) has merged**". PR #14775 reads `merged: true`, `merged_at: 2026-09-03T09:53:29Z` — read from `merged_at`, which is the only authority for when something landed. The column therefore exists on `main` to have its `readonly` removed; the triage note at 5519692084 that measured `git grep 13881 -- packages/` → 0 predates that merge and is now stale.

`needs:contract-review` is hung on this card per the ruling's own `Clause-②: yes` (a published write path accepts a field it refused before); the PR carries it too, and this seat does not clear either carrier on its own certification.

> Claim: dispatched by the `domain:services` execution seat, PM session `session_01AUF1NoViznQK32gqpK8wS8`. Delivering PR #14958 on branch `claude/issue-14787-user-writable-locale`.

## Provenance — a respelling, and the ruling's own reading

Not a new judgement. **Maintainer ruling B** (comment 5522882528, verbatim 「同意」) sets `Clause-②: yes` itself, on the grounds that *a published write path accepts a field it refused before*. My earlier claim comment carried that reading only as inline prose inside a sentence, which `CLAUSE2_KEY_LINE` — line-anchored, exactly `Clause-②: yes` or `Clause-②: no` — reads as **nothing**.

The dev re-derived it independently from its own diff and agrees, stating the concrete before/after: a user-context `PATCH /api/v1/data/sys_user/:id` carrying `locale` was answered with `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` (or had the key stripped) on `main`, and now commits.

⇒ Three sources agree — the ruling, the dev's re-derivation, and the mechanical bar. `yes`.

## Both carriers, and one was genuinely half-written

`check-clause2-carriers.mjs --pair 14958` also raised **C1**: the card carried `needs:contract-review` while the delivering PR did **not**. That was a real half-state on my side — I pre-hung the card at dispatch per the ruling, and the PR did not exist yet; when it opened at 12:56Z the hang never reached it. Now hung on both.

The checker's note on why the second carrier is not decoration is worth repeating rather than paraphrasing: it is *"the only machine-readable evidence that a gate was CLEARED rather than STRIPPED — a legitimate clear leaves two removals seconds apart, a strip leaves one"*, and since 「闸门被剥不是红灯是放行」, 「被剥」 and 「从未挂过」 are otherwise indistinguishable in the evidence.

⚠️ Standing consequence: ⛔ this PR is **not** to be undrafted or armed on CI colour alone. The contract review gates it, and this seat does not self-certify at a lower tier.
